utterances.text: Let us clarify. It is up to the Judges to clarify the debate. What is the aim that you are pursuing, Mr. Nobilo, by asking the witness to comment on this document? Let us make it very clear. Otherwise, I will write a written brief to tell you what I think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is very simple, Mr. President. I am surprised by my learned colleague. We are talking about this document. On the second page, Zenica is mentioned, that there was talk of the shelling of Zenica. But it is not said that Stewart said that, and that is what is missing. We just wanted to say that this document is original, is authentic, but that a part is missing. We don't know how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have said that and then we will go on. The decision of the Chamber was very clear. You will ask the accused, who is the witness today, what is missing and what is not. We are not going to go back to this whole conversation with Colonel Stewart, that it is a crime against humanity, et cetera, et cetera. So please, Mr. Nobilo, go to the essentials because you have gone beyond your time. I want to remind you of that. So let us go on to the next document unless you have something very specific to ask of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have nothing further, but if the witness claims that something is missing from the document, it's logical for me to ask him what is missing. But let us go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, quite logic. I said what is my right to say, but it is logic. Since the beginning of this conversation, when you chose to go through a chronology minute by minute by the accused, you may have avoided making a point of the important issues, but that was your choice. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. We have finished with this document. The next one we would like to show you is the statement of Mr. Payam Akhavan, and my colleague will read some excerpts from certain pages and we will ask the witness to comment on the statement of this Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, no. No, no, no. Not at all, Mr. Nobilo. You will put the document on the ELMO, and you will draw the attention of your client to a particular point that you wish him to react on. We are not going to read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am referring to three sentences. Unfortunately, the witness doesn't speak English, so we see no way of getting around it. This is very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Registrar. It is not an exhibit, Mr. President. We are putting pages of the transcript of the trial on the ELMO. I don't think they need to be marked, to save time. We will put the page and line numbers in the record. It will be perfectly clear what we're referring to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Hayman. Let us go on, and after that, we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I ask Mr. Hayman to read it? He will do so better than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: First, we're reading from transcript page 5296, beginning at line 22, and this, for the Court's information, this is the testimony of Payam Akhavan, referring to then Colonel Blaskic. "He suggested to me that although there may have been some paramilitary formations that he was clearly in command of the Lasva Valley region and that no operation of any military significance could take place either without his consent or his knowledge."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, your comment?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the knowledge that I had at the time, I think this was the 4th of May, 1993, I provided an answer to Mr. Akhavan indicating what I knew at that point in time, that the units subordinated to me had not carried out any combat operations without my knowledge and order or, rather, that I had not ordered the operations which resulted in the crime in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you say that no significant military operation could be carried out without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know who had been the perpetrators of the operation, but I believed at the time that I must have known about any military operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't understand. You do not disagree with this sentence, General Blaskic; you agree with this statement by Mr. Akhavan. What you wanted to say is that you added something else to that dialogue?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I agree that all units under my command, my units, could not have carried out an operation without my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Then you agree with this statement. There's no problem. I understand. You want to add to this transcript. I see very well. But we have to be very careful, Mr. Nobilo. Does the witness agree or not with this statement, that is, that no significant military operation could take place without his knowledge? Are you in agreement with that statement? You were the chief. Fine. What you wanted to say is simply that this doesn't apply to Ahmici, if I understand well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us look at some other quotations from Mr. Akhavan's testimony, then it will become clearer, because there is a difference in understanding between Mr. Akhavan and Mr. Blaskic as to which are his units. This is a question of terminological misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Transcript page 5332, line 5 to line 12. "Q Am I correct that in the course of this meeting with Colonel Blaskic, he denied ordering the killing of any civilians in Ahmici or anywhere else; is that correct? A Correct. Q Did he also deny that he knew in advance that any civilians would be killed in Ahmici or anywhere else; correct? A Correct."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. Is it necessary for the accused to explain that particular question and answer? Is that what's being explored here? If it is, we object, if this is the method that is being explored. Now, if there is some terminological problem in a question and answer, that is a different issue, but I trust that there is no terminological problem with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with Mr. Kehoe. Either there is a terminological problem or there is a witness who said this. It is up to you, in the time allotted to you, or in your final argument, to refer to ambiguities, but we are not going -- in a civil law system, Mr. Nobilo, that you are familiar with, there is a confrontation, but we are not in that system. For the moment, we have the transcript of the statement of a Prosecution witness which you are commenting on. It is sufficient for you to say that you contest this sentence and we can go on to another document. If not, Mr. Akhavan is not here. I really don't see why -- perhaps we will have to add to the Court witnesses Mr. Akhavan. This becomes very complicated, applying your method. Do you understand what I'm saying, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, but it seemed to us that if certain witnesses have certain precise knowledge about their contacts with General Blaskic, then it is much easier for the Court if General Blaskic himself comments on the statements of those witnesses. There is not a lot of that. We felt that it would be better for General Blaskic to explicitly dispute or confirm key sentences by certain Prosecution witnesses rather than the Court having to look through the whole transcript to find these places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges will do their work, let me assure you, Mr. Nobilo. I understand very well that you wish to have your client's reaction to such and such a point, but it is quite sufficient for your client to give us his reaction very quickly instead of starting a debate about a phrase, a sentence by a witness who came I don't know how long ago and was examined by the Prosecution. Go directly to the point, and your client will say, "I agree. I have such and such a thing to add," or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I simply wanted to ask the witness whether he agreed and he would have answered "Yes" or "No" and we would have finished with this. That is all that I had wanted to ask him about this sentence. I just wanted to ask him whether he agrees that that was what was stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. As it is your attorney that is asking you this question, give us a "Yes" or "No" answer and we will go on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you agree that you said what Mr. Hayman has just read out? Now you don't remember what it was that Mr. Hayman read out. We have to repeat it because the witness cannot remember what it was that was read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic is right. There was quite a long period of discussion between us. So let us read it again for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Transcript page 5332, lines 5 to 12. "Q Am I correct that in the course of this meeting with Colonel Blaskic, he denied ordering the killing of any civilians in Ahmici or anywhere else; is that correct? A Correct. Q Did he also deny that he knew in advance that any civilians would be killed in Ahmici or anywhere else; correct? A Correct."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this a correct representation of the conversation with you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Shall we go on to the next document or, Mr. President, shall we have a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. Mr. Nobilo, how many transcripts of that kind do you want to submit to the General?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think about five, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We don't think it's normal that you have to show the transcripts that way to the General. Let me remind you that you had the possibility, during the cross-examination, to challenge what the different witnesses had said, and the witnesses were present at that time. Mr. Akhavan, for instance, when he came to testify, you had the opportunity to challenge his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And we did do so, but at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you did so, it is now in the transcript, but you had the possibility to call the witness if you wished to do so, but you didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But at the time, the witness, General Blaskic, did not make a testimony, and we were not able to confront his testimony with that of Mr. Akhavan because General Blaskic was not presenting his defence at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's the same difficulty. Mr. Akhavan is not here in the courtroom. We cannot confront Mr. Akhavan with what General Blaskic says. So I'm wondering if this procedure is normal. You had the opportunity to call the accused as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, but we are not doing this confrontation between two witnesses, as is usually done in continental law. That is not what we're doing. We are questioning our own witness but with the help of the material that we have at our disposal, and the material is either evidence or the statements of witnesses who have already testified. So it's just helping us to ask these questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but we can ask this question for the transcript. Is this a normal procedure? Mr. Prosecutor, would you like to make some comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The thing that is extremely odd in the scenario, Mr. President, is that there was discussion about all of these meetings, such as the meeting with Mr. Akhavan, during the course of this chronology that we went through. Just as there was discussion about the meeting with Colonel Stewart, there was a long discussion about what was said during this meeting with Mr. Akhavan. Clearly, during the context of that meeting, should there be some discrepancy as to who meant what or there's some terminological problem, that would be the logical place to bring it out. Now we are going back over ground that we went over before, such as that "I didn't mean --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Not only did you face this contradiction -- didn't you face this contradiction during cross-examination, but you're saying yes. Okay. I'll accept that answer. But I was about to add this: The accused chose to testify chronologically, so when he mentioned the day of the 20th or 24th of April, he should have said, "To this regard, I would like to make more precise that I did say that during that day but that I didn't say something else." He should have said it that way and at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we are forbidden from raising something because it wasn't brought out in chronological order, the Court may so order and preclude us from going into these matters, but we would object to that, of course. We collected these items together because we thought it would be more efficient to do it in this way. We highlighted the specific words we wanted to bring to the witness's attention. We will proceed or we will stop, if the Court orders us to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you won't have the pleasure to express an official objection showing that the rights of the accused were violated. Let me note that they weren't violated before. We will apply the standards of international law, however, the international standards of the common law. According to these standards, the Prosecution and the Defence are on an equal footing. Moreover, our Rules state that the Judges must make sure that the trial takes place expeditiously. But given the fact that there are five transcripts, we will follow the method used by the Judges a few moments ago. You will show the excerpt of the transcript to the witness. We will ask General Blaskic to give a very concise and brief answer. If General Blaskic or his defence counsel didn't have time to express their objections when they should have, that is, during the cross-examination of the Prosecution witness, and because the Defence counsel did not call the accused to the witness stand when it was possible and because you used a chronology, a very lengthy method, you will recognise this, but which had the advantage of shedding some light on all the important points and, however, today we have to shed some light on different points. However, the Judges have decided to maintain their previous position. Mr. Nobilo, you can show the excerpt of the transcript you're interested in, and I will ask General Blaskic to give a very short answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The text is already on the ELMO, and I will ask my learned colleague to read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The testimony of Payam Akhavan, transcript page 5299, lines 7 through 13, partial: "At the end of the interview, I asked Colonel Blaskic who could have possibly committed the attacks on civilians in Ahmici as well as Vitez, and he was not really able to give me any alternative explanation. He simply told me that he did not know who did it, and he was certain that his own soldiers did not."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, would you explain? Is that correct and what did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, what I said is correct. Under my soldiers, I always implied soldiers who were directly subordinate to me in terms of command and control. That was the practice, and we all used that practice in the HVO and in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will remind you that the accused had already said that on numerous or various occasions, so maybe it was not necessary after all. But it's your choice. Go on. Next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No. We've finished with that. I now propose that the witness be handed Prosecution Exhibit 380. It is the interview in the paper called Danas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, this document, have you seen it in the course of your examination?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I have not seen this document, apart from when I saw it in court when it was offered to the other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, what is "Danas"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "Danas," meaning "today" is a journal in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The author of the interview is Slobodan Lovrenovic. Who was he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, he worked in the IPD in Mostar attached to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is "IPD"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This document has never been presented before? Wasn't it presented recently?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was presented on the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It was presented yesterday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, not our witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This document was introduced during the testimony of Brigadier Alastair Duncan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, General Blaskic ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, before coming to the courtroom, did you ever see this interview before?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: IPD, Lovrenovic, an officer that worked at the IPD. What is IPD?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: IPD is the Military Information and Propaganda Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell the Court, please, in clear terms, did you give this interview?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How did it come into being?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, they sent questions via telefax for the interview, and that was sometime at the end of September, beginning of October, at the time when the conflicts were fiercest, and I only wrote out the theses, and the complete integral interview was written by my assistant for IPD in the Operative Zone command for Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: IPD programme, did it incorporate the writing of texts in the name of the commander which were to be made public?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, they were texts which were published, and the aim of them was to raise morale and propaganda for one's own forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The complete text, was it shown to you or sent for your authorisation before it was published?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was never shown to me nor was it given to me to be authorised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, we should now like to show a statement disclosed at a closed session, so we would like to propose that we go into a private session. No? Closed session? No, we have to have a closed session because, on the ELMO, it would be evident who the witness is, the page number, et cetera. The topic is a question which was never raised with General Blaskic nor was the testimony of this witness discussed with General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Closed session, please. A closed session or a private session? Closed session. Well, let's move into a closed session then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
